statements.text: China has paused restrictions on key elements like dysprosium, gadolinium, terbium, yttrium, and more — vital to EVs, defense tech & semiconductors.
After the U.S. dropped tariffs on Chinese goods from 145% to 30%, and China slashed tariffs from 125% to 10%, this suspension followed as a goodwill gesture.

On July 26, 2025, the U.S. and China announced that the two countries had reached a deal to accelerate the import of rare earth elements (REEs) and the magnets they are used in, into the U.S. from China.
The new restrictions apply to 7 of 17 REEs—samarium, gadolinium, terbium, dysprosium, lutetium, scandium, and yttrium—and requires companies to secure special export licenses
The agreement will be implemented once it is approved by President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

On April 4, 2024, China responded to U.S. tariffs, which at the time were 145% on certain imports, and up to 245% on other products, by placing export restrictions on seven REEs – samarium, gadolinium, terbium, dysprosium, lutetium, scandium, and yttrium
